statement: A case report of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) described a 10-year-old Pakistani boy who presented with a 6-month history of pain and tender masses on the back, left arm, and left hip; the pain was insidious, gradually worsened, and caused difficulty walking and decreased range of motion of the shoulders and hips.

statement: A case report of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) described a sixteen-year-old male patient who presented with complaints of pain and swelling in his upper back, where a biopsy had been performed two months before; at age 9, he developed tender stiffness of his shoulders and neck, and over the next 4 years experienced multiple similar swellings on the upper back, with limited movement of the shoulders and neck and progressive masses.

statement: FOP is caused by heterozygous activating mutations in activin A receptor, type I/activin-like kinase 2 (ACVR1/ALK2), and DNA sequence analysis of ACVR1/ALK2 can confirm the diagnosis of FOP.

statement: In individuals with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), trauma to the muscles, such as a fall or invasive medical procedures, may trigger episodes of muscle swelling and inflammation (myositis) followed by more rapid ossification in the injured area.
